claim: The owner ruled, after the harness kit's first pull request was opened with the set-up and the parallel commands still in JavaScript: the kit is for the second person, who follows the README, runs one thing and has it work without hassle; the set-up and the parallel commands are shifted to Rust; JavaScript that was built for the kit and then replaced by Rust is a duplicate and is removed; settings of this PC that give an advantage are added to the kit; small, easy fixes among the open points are made; the kit and its report do not speak of this PC; and the work must not take long. He raised the job's cap from 100 M to 140 M tokens for it.
when: about to leave a JavaScript version in the kit beside its Rust replacement, to describe the kit in terms of the owner's PC, to leave a helpful setting of this PC out of the kit's set-up, or to list a small fix for later instead of making it
quote: if it's a duplicate sitting in the kit, just remove it since it's a duplicate and it isn't contributing anything

claim: The harness kit after the Rust-only round of 2026-11-25 (commit 19d85582 on bilal/build); the command names and the JavaScript files named in r58-0108 are replaced as said here. A second person needs the Rust toolchain and git only. The set-up is the program kit-setup, started by harness-kit/setup.sh or setup.cmd (--apply, --remove, --status, --project, --no-usage-tool, --fetch); it builds the workspace, wires the six hook programs into the project's settings.local.json and also writes, only where she has no value of her own and recorded so that --remove takes out exactly those: CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT 0 (helpers of helpers in the background, r57-0157), the Opus window of 400 K the window ceiling's lines were measured under (r57-0107), and in the clone the trimmed skill listing. The parallel commands are the programs kit-queue (the queue for heavy commands), kit-check (test files side by side, a measuring run) and kit-unit (units in their own copies, landing through the check, undone on a failure); the token counter is kit-tokens. Removed as duplicates: harness-kit/setup.mjs, setup.test.mjs, tokens.mjs, hooks/kit-start.mjs, parallel/unit.mjs, check.mjs, kitlib.mjs and .claude/hooks/kit-mode.mjs; the four JavaScript hooks that had been given a kit mode are again byte for byte what main holds. Tests: kit-setup 22 cargo tests holding the 58 ported cases and 7 new; the parallel commands' test file 6 of 6 against the programs; the hooks' test files against the programs: window-ceiling 135, creep-gate 42, count-gate 30, fanout-gate 49, tier hook 30 with 1 skipped, start hook 10, token counter 8. Two small fixes: tier-hook.mjs looks a kind up only among the routes file's own kinds, so a description starting 'constructor:' is refused instead of passing unchecked (point 1 of r58-0500); an effort check in kit-tier-hook, on trial: in kit mode a helper start must name an effort its route allows (routes file, from the design of r57-0207), each decision logged with the effort (point 4). Points 2, 3 and 5 of r58-0500 are not part of the kit and stay open. node harness-kit/check-clone.mjs passed every line after the round. Two of the round's five builders were again stopped by the migration gate's repair-loop rule (counts 0, 3, 3) and finished by a fresh helper. Per-builder tokens are in research-tree/build/KIT-ENFORCE-STATE.md. Not run: macOS and Linux, a live session on the wired programs, the pytest defaults.
